resources.string: A panel at the screen edge: apps and an LG TV remote, one pull away
Pull the handle inwards or tap it
Pull the bar at the screen edge inwards and the panel comes out with your finger. A tap opens it too. Drag the bar up or down to move it.
Once started, a thin bar stays at the screen edge, on top of every app.
Turn on “Display over other apps” so the bar and panel can show on top of other apps, then come back.
Drag the bar up or down with your finger; its place is saved.
Handle moved back to its default place
Tick the apps for the panel. The order you tick them is their order in the panel.
You can choose up to %1$d apps
This phone has an infrared emitter
This phone has no infrared emitter
This phone has no infrared emitter; the TV remote cannot work.
Point the top edge of the phone at the TV. The power key sends the LG remote\'s power code; the HDMI keys use LG\'s direct input codes. You can try them here with the buttons below.
Needed for the bar and the panel
A small notification stays while the panel is on
So it keeps running in the background
Turn on “Display pop-up windows while running in the background” and autostart so the panel can open apps
Edge Panel · Talks only to the TV at home, nothing else.
The panel follows your finger while you pull and springs open when you let go. Its contents come in one after another and keys squeeze and ripple. The background is not blurred, only slightly dimmed.
This screen goes up to %1$d Hz. %2$d Hz is requested while pulling and while the panel is open, then back to normal.
This screen goes up to %1$d Hz; animations run at that rate (90 FPS needs a 90 Hz screen).
The phone and the TV must be on the same Wi-Fi. It connects by itself while the panel opens and finds the TV again if its address changes.
No Android TV paired yet. Pair once; after that it connects by itself.
Touchpad: swipe to move, tap to select
✓ Paired with %1$s. The panel now connects by itself.
Pairing is done once. The phone\'s key is kept only inside this app and is never backed up; only the TV at home is contacted.
If the TV is not found: on the TV, Settings → Network & Internet → your Wi-Fi: type its IP address here.
No Android TV found. Is the TV on and on the same Wi-Fi? You can also add it by IP address below.
Looking for Android TVs on the Wi-Fi…
Wrong code. The TV will show a new code…
Pair once; then it connects by itself.
The TV does not know this phone.
%1$s does not answer. Is the TV on and on the same Wi-Fi as the phone? Its address may have changed: pick it from the list again or type the IP again.
%1$s refused the connection. The TV\'s \"Android TV Remote Service\" may be off or outdated: on the TV, Play Store → \"Android TV Remote Service\" → Update.

The \"Android TV Remote Service\" on %1$s is outdated. On the TV, open the Play Store, search for \"Android TV Remote Service\" and press Update (older devices such as the Mi Box 4 do not update it by themselves). Then tap Try again.
Could not set up a secure connection with %1$s. Restart the TV and try again.
%1$s refused pairing. On the TV: Settings → Apps → System apps → Android TV Remote Service → Clear data, then try again.
Allow access once to control music.

Shows the song playing in apps like YouTube Music, with its buttons, in the panel. Notifications are not read or stored. If the switch is greyed out: Settings → Apps → Kenar Panel → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings.
